output.answer: Raycon (Raycon Global Inc., the New York wireless-earbuds brand) is a privately held company. It was co-founded in 2017 by the entertainer Ray J (William Ray Norwood Jr.) and Ray Lee, but Ray J no longer owns any of it: on March 6, 2024 Raycon announced he was 'stepping away from his role as an officer and shareholder by fully divesting his shares of Raycon in a company buyback' to launch a television venture, Tronix Network. As of 2026 reporting, ownership is described as consolidated around co-founder/CEO Ray Lee and company management, with no publicly disclosed outside investors. Some secondary sources claim GoDigital Media Group, a privately held media conglomerate founded by Jason Peterson, acquired Raycon in March 2024, but that claim is not supported by a primary source: GoDigital's own site does not mention Raycon, and Wikipedia's list of GoDigital subsidiaries omits it, so the current precise cap table cannot be confirmed from public records.
caveats: Conflicting secondary accounts of current ownership: LegalClarity (June 2026) and TheZeroNet report that GoDigital Media Group acquired Raycon outright in March 2024, while RevenueMemo's 2026 ownership explainer says ownership consolidated around Ray Lee and management with no disclosed outside investors and calls secondary claims of private holding entities as majority owners 'unverified.'

No primary source confirming a GoDigital acquisition was located: GoDigital's own website does not mention Raycon, and Wikipedia's GoDigital Media Group subsidiary list (AdShare, Cinq Music, ContentBridge, GoDigital, Media Aggregators, Latido Networks, mitu, Sound Royalties, YogaWorks) omits Raycon as of retrieval on 2026-11-11.
Raycon is private and discloses no ownership percentages; the exact split among remaining shareholders is not publicly confirmed, and no SEC filing exists because the company was never public.
The value of Ray J's divested stake was never disclosed; contemporaneous reports estimated anywhere from about $35-45 million up to $85-100 million.

passages.quote: NEW YORK, March 6, 2024 /PRNewswire/ -- [Raycon](https://c212.net/c/link/?t=0&l=en&o=4109537-1&h=789803218&u=http%3A%2F%2Fwww.rayconglobal.com%2F&a=Raycon), the premier Everyday Tech brand designing reliable, accessible and delightful consumer products, today announces that to pursue his first personal passion in television, co-founder Ray J is stepping away from his role as an officer and shareholder by fully divesting his shares of Raycon in a company buyback.

Raycon is privately held and controlled by co-founder and chief executive Ray Lee, together with company management. It has no publicly disclosed outside investors. Co-founder Ray J left the company and sold his shares in March 2024.

Shortly after Ray J’s departure, Raycon announced on March 19, 2024 that it had been acquired by GoDigital Media Group. GoDigital describes itself as a privately held multinational conglomerate that operates across music, video, content licensing, and consumer brands.3GoDigital Media Group. [GoDigital Media Group](https://godigital.com/) Its portfolio includes music distribution, royalty financing, and [intellectual property](https://legalclarity.org/intellectual-property-ip-types-rights-and-protection/) businesses.

The music/television star and entrepreneur has [exited his post at Raycon Global](https://thejasminebrand.com/2024/03/07/exclusive-ray-j-departs-raycon-sells-shares-to-launch-massive-tv-platform-tronix-network/) despite its $300 million in revenue, _The Jasmine Brand_ reported. Insiders say the _Love & Hip Hop_ star has his sights set on media expansion in the form of a massive entertainment platform dubbed Tronix Network.

No institutional investors in Raycon have been confirmed. There are no disclosed venture firms, private equity holders, or corporate minority stakeholders on the public record as of 2026. Some secondary sources name private holding entities as majority owners, but none of those claims is supported by primary reporting or company disclosure, so they should be treated as unverified.

output.question: Who owns Raycon?

key_facts.fact: Raycon was co-founded in 2017 by Ray J (William Ray Norwood Jr.) and Ray Lee, based in New York City; the brand name blends their first names.

Raycon announced that co-founder Ray J was stepping away as officer and shareholder, fully divesting his shares via a company buyback to pursue his television venture Tronix Network; Ray Lee is Raycon CEO.
Black Enterprise reported Ray J sold his complete portfolio of Raycon Global shares, with insiders estimating his proceeds at $35-45 million to possibly $85-100 million.
As of 2026, Raycon is privately held and controlled by co-founder and CEO Ray Lee together with company management, with no publicly disclosed outside investors; Ray J holds no equity or role.
LegalClarity reports Raycon announced on March 19, 2024 that it had been acquired by GoDigital Media Group, a privately held multinational conglomerate; purchase terms were not disclosed.
LegalClarity (published June 12, 2026) states GoDigital Media Group acquired Raycon in March 2024 and that Ray J had fully divested his shares, leaving the company under new ownership.
